question: What is continuous small-batch v11 TimeSeries write and merge amplification for default LowCardinality(UUID) versus raw UUID ID when most series repeat across batches?
baseline: Unmodified stock O1 ClickHouse 26.11.1.1, build 41596421285, executable SHA256 f0a2fa1f814c58853f43423705cac10ab9df3bfe5887e27ebe9620ba7cb9660e; TimeSeries v11 default LowCardinality UUID ID
candidate: Same binary and source, only explicit Tuple(UInt64,UUID) inner ID type on TAGS/SAMPLES/TimeRanges; hash expression and text index unchanged
fixture: Deterministic synthetic input, 400 stable slots, 400 rotating slots, 12 batches, 60s steps, rotating quarter-life at batch 3/6/9; generator SHA and exact sample/series oracle; two tables read identical input
single_variable: Only internal ID column type LC UUID vs raw UUID; same stock O1 binary, same data, no source patch
math_bound: For N physical ID references in each part and D distinct IDs, uncompressed dictionary encodes roughly 16D+wN vs raw 16N bytes (w index width). Benefit requires D/N << 1 and actual compressed bytes; CPU for dictionary decoding, insert and merges can negate byte saving. Counting inserted sample points != bucketed SAMPLES rows; require sum(length(samples)) and exact native query parity.
falsifier: Different physical sample points, wrong UUID identity or native values; >25% paired baseline drift; unexpected global RSS OOM; candidate worsens write CPU/merge CPU/disk at high repeat ratio, or true background merge cost unmeasurable
test_matrix: 12 chronological small batches of stable/rotating IDs, two v11 TimeSeries physical schemas, each batch interleaved A/B, forced merge controls, query_log per INSERT, system.part_log merge stats if available, physical part bytes, sum(length(samples)), native avg-over-time parity on stage and whole queries before/after merges
runner_budget: One small local source+binary smoke, then <=25min isolated GitHub Actions measurement with stock O1 SHA-verified binary, 1 job, no compilation
planned_workflow: .github/workflows/ts-lab-r02-small-batch-write-20261103.yml path-isolated push, run-unique concurrency, no schedule
